previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with abdominal pain, nausea, and diabetic ketoacidosis after not eating for six days and stopping insulin due to dizziness. She initially refused exams and labs but gradually engaged in care. Treatment included IV fluids, correction of DKA, and continuation of her oral pain regimen without IV narcotics. Her insulin was adjusted after discovering a dosing error with U500, and she was stabilized on a lower subcutaneous regimen. She resumed oral intake without pain exacerbation, and her dizziness resolved. Imaging showed no acute abdominal pathology. She was discharged home with updated insulin instructions, follow-up appointments, and continuation of her chronic pain and psychiatric medications.
problems: Diabetes with ketoacidosis, type I [juvenile type], uncontrolled
